method: Independent mathematical analysis of actual official statements. No inaccessible editorial is claimed read.

reviews.statement_summary: Colored rooted tree,N,Q<=100000; count colors occurring at least k times in a queried subtree.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Flatten subtrees to Euler intervals and order offline queries with Mo. Maintain freq[color] and atLeast[t],the number of colors reaching threshold t. Adding changes only atLeast[newFreq] by+1; removing changes only atLeast[oldFreq] by-1. Answer atLeast[k] in O(1); total about O((N+Q)sqrtN) moves. Count colors,not vertices; k above subtree size yields0.

reviews.statement_summary: Manager forest,N,Q<=100000; count other vertices sharing a queried p-th ancestor with v.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Binary-lift v by p. If no real ancestor exists return0; otherwise count vertices of depth[v] inside that ancestor's Euler interval using two binary searches in the depth's sorted tin list,and subtract v itself. Equal depths ensure that ancestor is p steps above every counted vertex. O((N+Q)logN); do not count the virtual forest root as an ancestor.

reviews.statement_summary: Labeled rooted tree,N,Q<=500000; can letters at absolute depth h in subtree v be permuted into a palindrome?
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: For each depth store Euler entry times and prefix XORs of26-bit character parity masks. Two binary searches isolate the subtree range; its XOR has at most one set bit iff a palindrome exists. Empty ranges satisfy the condition. O((N+Q)logN); root depth is1 and subtree includes its root.

reviews.statement_summary: Tree queries ask how many vertices have equal distances to two given vertices.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: If endpoints coincide answer N; if their distance is odd answer0. Otherwise find the midpoint c by LCA/lifting. Remove the two components reached from c toward the endpoints; every remaining vertex projects to c on the endpoint path and is equidistant. Branch size is child subtree size or N-size[c] for the parent direction. O(logN) per query.

reviews.statement_summary: A tree has people with distinct IDs at cities; each query asks for up to10 smallest IDs on a path.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Store the smallest10 IDs on each upward binary-lifting segment. Merging truncated lists is safe: an item discarded from one list is already dominated by10 items there. Decompose both path sides into disjoint segments,merge and truncate,and include LCA once. O(10logN) per query; cities may be empty or contain many people.

reviews.statement_summary: Connected simple weighted graph,N,M<=200000; for each edge find minimum spanning-tree weight when that edge is mandatory.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Build an MST of weight W by Kruskal and preprocess maximum-edge queries on its paths with LCA. Adding edge(u,v,w) creates a cycle; remove its maximum-weight original path edge. Exchange/cut optimality gives W+w-maxPath(u,v),including W for MST edges. O(MlogM+(N+M)logN); use64-bit total and preserve input edge order.

reviews.statement_summary: Initially a forest; answer component diameters and optimally merge two components by choosing any connecting endpoints.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Precompute each tree diameter. Store diameters on DSU roots. An optimal new edge joins centers,so merged diameter=max(d1,d2,ceil(d1/2)+ceil(d2/2)+1). Radius bounds prove necessity and center connection attains it. Same-component merges do nothing. Initial traversal O(N+M),then amortized DSU cost; query vertices identify components,not forced edge endpoints.

reviews.statement_summary: Orient every edge of a connected simple undirected graph to make it strongly connected,or output0.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: A bridge makes strong orientation impossible. DFS orients tree edges downward and non-tree edges toward ancestors. Without bridges each child subtree has a back route to an ancestor,so every vertex reaches root while downward tree edges reach all vertices. Low-link bridge detection and orientation take O(N+M); preserve one output per edge and use iterative DFS for deep inputs.

reviews.statement_summary: Classify each edge as in every MST,some but not all,or no MST; equal-weight ties matter.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Process equal-weight groups together using a DSU of strictly lighter edges. Internal edges are none. Contract DSU roots and find bridges in the group's multigraph: bridges are mandatory,other remaining edges optional. Only then union the whole group. Even a simple input can create parallel contracted edges,so bridge DFS must use edge IDs. O(MlogM+M alphaN).

reviews.statement_summary: Power every city by stations or Manhattan-priced wires;N<=2000,output total,stations and connections.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Add a virtual source with edge cost c[i] to each city; city-city edge cost is Manhattan distance*(k[i]+k[j]). Connecting all vertices to the source exactly models powered components. An MST is optimal; dense Prim computes edge costs on demand in O(N²),without storing all edges. Source-parent edges become stations.64-bit costs; coincident cities permit zero-cost wires.

reviews.statement_summary: Array length2^n,n<=17; alternating OR and XOR reductions define root value; report it after each point assignment.
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Build a complete segment tree with OR at height1 above leaves,XOR at height2,and alternating thereafter. A point change affects only its ancestor chain. Keep operation tied to segment height,not global update count. Build O(2^n),each update O(n); check n1 versus n2 root operation.

reviews.statement_summary: For each range of an array,N,Q<=200000,compute sum over values of value*frequency².
reviews.solution_proof_and_edge_cases: Mo ordering converts queries to endpoint add/remove updates. Adding value x at old count f increases answer by x*(2f+1); removing at old f changes it by x*(1-2f). Keep64-bit answer and frequency arrays; alternating right-end ordering improves constants. Roughly O((N+Q)sqrtN) moves; restore original query order.
